pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Media - pass structs by reference instead of by value
pr_body:
Change the MCC (media control client) and media proxy APIs to pass structs by reference instead of by value.
- optimization - less to pass around
- consistency - this is how structs are usually passed in comparable files

Note that these APIs are marked as experimental, so API changes should be OK.

Also changes internal functions in the media player, the media client test, and the media controller test to pass structs by reference instead of by value.

closes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/42096
pr_comments: Does this also consider whether the function needs to modify the parameter, and if not use `const struct foo *`?

> Does this also consider whether the function needs to modify the parameter, and if not use `const struct foo *`?

No, that was forgotten.  Will fix.

Updated with 'const' keywords where appropriate (=everywhere).
Added a couple of small commits to allow  to make all structs const.

Added CHECKIF to the places where user/application code submits structs by reference.
Added `const` structs to a couple of more internal calls.
Fix commit message that did not pass compliance - use correct format for reference to other commit.

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Media: Pass structs by reference and not value
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
There are a few structs in the media implementation where the structs are passed by value, instead of reference. In smaller structs that may be OK, but there are structs > sizeof(pointer), where it definitely shouldn't be the case. Furthermore, for consistency we may want to just pass all structs, regardless of size, by reference instead of value. 

Specific examples are the `struct mpl_cmd_ntf` and `struct mpl_cmd`, but there may be others. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Basically change uses of the structs from e.g. 
```c
typedef void (*bt_mcc_cmd_ntf_cb)(struct bt_conn *conn, int err, struct mpl_cmd_ntf ntf);
```
to
```c
typedef void (*bt_mcc_cmd_ntf_cb)(struct bt_conn *conn, int err, struct mpl_cmd_ntf *ntf);
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
In some cases, we may just want to skip the smaller struct and just pass the fields, but that's doubtful. 

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments: Unrelated to the changes in this PR but it looks like we always override `ntf->result_code` before calling `media_proxy_pl_command_cb`. If that is the case, why do we even use a `mpl_cmd_ntf` as a parameter instead of just the `requested_opcode`, and then just create the `mpl_cmd_ntf` in the command handlers?

It is not over-ridden, it is set.
But yes, could do as you suggest.  It adds one more variable (opcode + `mpl_cmd_ntf` instead of just the last one), but maybe it looks cleaner.
I believe the thought was that the notification struct must be filled in with values from two places in the code, so it was just as easy to send it along.
No strong opinion on this one.

> It adds one more variable (opcode + mpl_cmd_ntf instead of just the last one),

If we send the opcode by parameter, we don't need the `mpl_cmd_ntf` argument at all, do we? 

mpl_cmd_ntf contains the opcode and a result code; if we get the opcode from the caller, and the result code from this function, this function can just allocate the `mpl_cmd_ntf` struct, right? 

It is outside the scope of this PR, so do with it as you will :)
